To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the microbiological response to therapy was similar in all treatment groups and that the microbiological profile was stable in the absence of periodontal therapy.

(i) the microbiological response to periodontal therapy in the absence of maintenance therapy is triphasic, with an initial precipitous decrease in the numbers and proportions of pathogens, a rise in numbers and proportions in the 3 months post therapy period, and a spontaneous decline over the 3 to 12 month period; and (ii) scaling and root planig (S) is more effective in reducing the proportions of detectable species than tetracycline fiber (F) therapy
the microbiological response of the six putative periodon- tal pathogens to the four periodontal therapies studied was characterized by a triphasic response.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel methods of delivering therapeutic agents to the periodontal pocket.
the study of the effect of the treatment of the disease.
developing new approaches to the study and management of periodontal diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
controlled release TC fibers are effective in decreasing levels of the monitored species in periodontitis patients.
the microbiological response to periodontal treatment is complex and multifaceted.

scaling and root planning (S), scaling, root planing and tetracycline fiber (TC) placement (SF), single TC fiber placement (F) and double TC fiber placement (FF) all significantly reduce periodontopathic microflora, with a triphasic response over a 12 month period.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of tetracycline fiber therapy in the treatment of periodontal disease results in a reduction of the number of periodontopathic bacteria.
the use of tetracycline in periodontal therapy is associated with significant microbiological changes in the periodontal pocket environment.
the microbiological response to periodontal treatment is a complex phenomenon, with a triphasic response of the periodontal microbiota.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we need to think about what is going to be best for the patient, not just what we are going to do for the patient.
we can use the data we have to make a decision.
there are many different kinds of periodontal diseases and the treatments for these conditions should be individualized to the specific needs of the patient.
